verdict.rationale: Cline's authorization docs list Bring Your Own Key as an option alongside signing in, so you can use your own provider credentials. The pricing page confirms you can bring API keys from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and others. The Cline provider page presents sign-in as the alternative to managing separate API keys, which implies key-based use does not need a Cline account login. Missing for 10: an explicit statement that no Cline account is required for BYOK, documentation of how keys are configured (e.g., CLI/headless env vars), and independent hands-on corroboration of key-only authentication.

support.subject: As a developer, I can authenticate with an API key instead of an account login

citations.quote: Bring Your Own Key (BYOK): use your own provider credentials (cloud or local runtimes).
You can bring your own API keys from providers like OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and others.
Instead of managing separate API keys across multiple vendors, you sign in once, add Cline credits, and select from available models directly in Cline.
